Are the OEM schema and verification VI files coming in a later update?

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/DEVELOPING.md#compatibility

Outright dropping a property isn't something we should really do.  Lets understand why this is providing the wrong value on your system and just fix it.  I'm not aware of this being wrong on other systems.

I'm aware of the compatibility thing that's why i asked on discord first if it's ok to drop the property.

Compatibility has to be weighed against passing redfish validation which is somewhat important when making patches which link various redfish resources.

When using the `Tree` validation the validator will follow links to other resources and at some point it will have queried the complete tree when starting from a resource with links. Not possible to pass the validator if any of these resources is wrong.

Essentially i won't be able to make changes to bmcweb as easily if there are redfish validator errors since passing the validator is part of your checklist.

I would have to disable the meson option for the OEM schema and run non default options.

#### inspection inside `asyncPopulatePid`

- at some point we arrive in `asyncPopulatePid`
- first it does `dbus::utility::getManagedObjects`
- we then proceed to interate over the result

```
   112             for (const auto& pathPair : managedObj)
   113             {
   114                 for (const auto& intfPair : pathPair.second)
```

and discard any interface which is not pid/zone/... related

```
   116                     if (intfPair.first != pidConfigurationIface &&
   117                         intfPair.first != pidZoneConfigurationIface &&
   118                         intfPair.first != stepwiseConfigurationIface)
   119                     {
   120                         continue;
   121                     }
```

after this check, further code in the loop is only processing object paths which have at least one of these interfaces on them.

Then a further check happens for pid zone config intf

```
   180                     if (intfPair.first == pidZoneConfigurationIface)
   181                     {
   182                         sdbusplus::message::object_path pidPath(
   183                             pathPair.first.str);
   184                         std::string chassis = pidPath.filename();
   185                         if (chassis.empty())
   186                         {
   187                             chassis = "#IllegalValue";
   188                         }
```

at that point it's clear we have a pid zone configuration intf on that object path.

> I'm not aware of this being wrong on other systems.

Can you kindly share your output of this endpoint + output of chassis collection.

Does your redfish chassis happen to be the same name as the PID zone?

Alternatively, the pid zone config intf would need to be on the same object path as the board/chassis interface which seems odd to me.

Taking a look at other deprecated properties, they usually provide reason/replacement for the deprecated property. Why would we be deprecating the property here? Do we have / need a replacement property?

(not counting myself).

Then why not just fix it here if we think we will use it one day?

Dropping it without schema changes seems like the least desirable choice to me.
Fixing it here or removing it completely (schema + implementation) seem like better paths to me.

Bumping the version to like OpenBMCManager.v1_1_0.Manager.FanZone will help clients handle this.

> Why have a property in the schema if we aren't going to use it?

There's tons of optional properties in redfish schemas that are not used in bmcweb. I had the impression that's kind of the default state for an optional property to be absent.

Anyways i resolved to fix the property instead of removing it since that's the outcome both you and Ed seem to be ok with.
I do think fixing this is the right answer vs outright removal.

I think I understand what's going on here.  Backend services have evolved, and now have more interfaces that might have string matches.  We weren't ever checking the interface names (because why would we) and we could not potentially point to a zone instead of a chassis.

Overall, I think this patch is headed in the right direction
